findings.current: “Your money is my money. My money isn’t my money, is it?”
findings.defect: The second sentence reverses the source negation and changes Jinho’s joke from claiming ownership of both men’s money to denying ownership of his own.
findings.rationale: 내 돈이 내 돈 아니냐 is a rhetorical affirmation meaning that his own money is, naturally, also his.
findings.replacement: “Your money is my money. And my money is my money, isn’t it?”
findings.source: “네 돈이 내 돈. 내 돈이 내 돈 아니냐.”

findings.current: “What are you talking about? Why did you suddenly cook ramen?”
findings.defect: The draft prematurely identifies ramen and turns Taekyung’s question into a request for a reason, making Jinho’s ensuing answer, “Obviously, ramen,” logically incoherent and weakening the misunderstanding that drives the joke.
findings.rationale: Taekyung is asking what Jinho suddenly means by talking about having cooked something; Jinho identifies that something as ramen in the next line.
findings.replacement: “What are you talking about? What’s this about cooking something all of a sudden?”

findings.current: He was someone I had lived with like a friend, like a brother, for several years.
findings.defect: “Lived with” implies that they shared a household or room, while the source says they had spent years relating to each other like friends and brothers.
findings.rationale: 지냈던 describes the relationship and time they spent together, not literal cohabitation.
findings.replacement: He was someone I’d spent years with, like a friend and a brother.
findings.source: 몇 년간 친구처럼, 형제처럼 지냈던 사람이다.

findings.current: “Damn it. How did you know? Even though you’re an F-rank Hunter…… Oh, right. You became C-rank a while ago.”
findings.defect: “Even though” is grammatically incomplete here and loses the contemptuous, teasing force of 주제에.
findings.rationale: F급 헌터 주제에 dismissively frames Taekyung as a mere F-rank Hunter before Jinho remembers his promotion.
findings.replacement: “Damn it. How did you know? You’re just an F-rank Hunter…… Oh, right. You became C-rank a while ago.”
findings.source: “젠장. 어떻게 알았지? F급 헌터 주제에…… 아, 너 얼마 전에 C급 됐지. 참.”

findings.current: I was an idiot for thinking about living with someone like him.
findings.defect: The draft softens the strong self-directed profanity 병신 and loses the force of Taekyung’s disgust with himself.
findings.rationale: 병신 is substantially stronger than the unmodified “idiot,” and the translation rules prohibit sanitizing strong profanity.
findings.replacement: I was a fucking idiot for thinking I could live with someone like him.
findings.source: 저런 인간하고 같이 살 생각을 한 내가 병신이지.

findings.current: “Samgyeopsal. Griddle barbecue. Fried chicken and beer.”
findings.defect: “Samgyeopsal” is left as an unestablished, unexplained romanization, while “griddle barbecue” is not idiomatic English.
findings.rationale: 삼겹살 is naturally conveyed as grilled pork belly, and 철판구이 denotes food cooked on an iron griddle, for which “teppanyaki” is the established English menu term.
findings.replacement: “Grilled pork belly. Teppanyaki. Fried chicken and beer.”

findings.current: “I’ve had enough of samgyeopsal and griddle barbecue. Let’s eat something pricier today.”
findings.defect: The repeated food terms retain the unexplained romanization and unnatural “griddle barbecue” wording.
findings.rationale: The food terminology should remain consistent with its first occurrence and read naturally in spontaneous dialogue.
findings.replacement: “I’m tired of grilled pork belly and teppanyaki. Let’s go for something pricier today.”
findings.source: “삼겹살이나 철판구이는 질렸다. 오늘은 좀 더 비싸게 먹어 보자꾸나.”

findings.current: His control of the burner flame for making a soft-boiled egg was good enough to call him a Peak master.
findings.defect: The egg was cracked directly into the ramen, so calling it “soft-boiled” inaccurately suggests an egg boiled in its shell.
findings.rationale: 반숙 here describes the desired soft-set, runny result of the raw egg cooking in the ramen.
findings.replacement: His control of the burner flame to leave the egg perfectly runny was worthy of a Peak master.
findings.source: 반숙을 만들기 위한 버너 화력 컨트롤은 절정 고수라고 해도 좋을 정도다.

findings.current: Look at that change of posture. Even Udyr would cry.
findings.defect: “Change of posture” is a literal calque that does not naturally express Jinho’s instant reversal from brazen demands to exaggerated submission.
findings.rationale: 태세 전환 figuratively means abruptly changing one’s attitude or position; “changing his tune” preserves the comic reversal in natural English.
findings.replacement: Talk about changing his tune. Even Udyr would weep.
findings.source: 태세 전환 봐라. 우디르도 울고 가겠다.

summary: Three substantive fidelity issues alter a negation, the ramen misunderstanding, and Taekyung’s relationship with Jinho. Additional findings concern lost contempt and profanity, food terminology, and localized wording.
